comment: Constants and per-archetype recipes of the building band planner (S2_ROOMS_PLAN.md sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.8; designer decision 8.1: minimum room 4 x 4 m). Read by Tools/TrainingGround/src/levelgen/buildings/bandPlan.ts. All lengths are integer cm in the planner's own frame (u along the long side, v across, v = 0 on the core wall). core.corridor_max_cm is a planner knob, not a plan constant: the widest the corridor may get beside the core in a double-loaded bay (it starts at the core depth and ends on the corridor line shared with the neighbouring bays).

window_vault.comment: Window vault data (lead addendum 2026-11-21; Tools/TrainingGround/src/levelgen/structureClasses.ts annotateWindowVault, schema /2 layouts): a window is vaultable when it is at least min_width_cm wide, its sill is one of the obstacle_heights.json classes in sill_classes (the mantle clip heights the obstacles are standardised to) and there is something to land on outside - the ground (storey 0), a balcony at the window or a walkable roof within roof_step_cm of the storey (probed probe_out_cm outside the wall).

office.bay_grammar: core room* (end | exit) | room* core room*

block.comment: S2.3 block (S2_ROOMS_PLAN.md 3.3 / 3.4): sections `flat core flat` (section_cm) or, under one section's minimum, `core flat` (the flat takes flat_bay_cm: L = 900 + flat); a landing (corridor cell) over the core bay at v = core depth .. landing_top (A / B boundary, one line for the whole building); per flat a back room A (depth = landing_top), a front room B (the rest) and the nearer front room C of the core bay (the core bay's front is split in two rooms of room_cm); the flat of one side per section gets a second entry through C (the section's loop), the other flat is a dead end. A long block is several sections side by side, a wall without doors between them (they meet on the roof). Per-storey slot windows (balcony / fire escape of story 4) sit in the B room of every flat from slot_min_storey up; designer 2026-11-19: no balcony without a fire escape, so no base balconies are generated.

templates.comment: Residential block plan templates (lead addendum 2026-11-21: several house types / eras - Stalin, brick, barracks, dormitory - are one data entry each). A building takes templates.default unless its spec names one (BuildingSpec.plan_template) or a series (BuildingSpec.series) that matches a template's series; GenBuilding.plan.template and GenBuilding.series / era record the choice. planner = the code that reads the entry: 'kit_sections' (buildings/kitPlan.ts: sections round a court-side core, flats with hall / bath / kitchen / living rooms) or 'sections' (the S2.3 planner, bandPlan.ts planBlock, numbers in recipes.block itself). A new template of an existing planner is a JSON entry only; storey_cm other than 300 needs a per-building storey height in the generator / builder (LEVEL_HEIGHT, z_of) - not wired yet.

block_khrushchevka.comment: Template block_khrushchevka (series 1-464, the 1960s five-storey panel block - the kit pattern of docs/design/levelgen/BGEN_KIT_PLANS_2026-11-21.md). Kit pattern of the residential block (docs/design/levelgen/BGEN_KIT_PLANS_2026-11-21.md; measured from the Soviet panel-block pack: KIT_PILOT_2026-11-20.md, Saved/KitDump). Chosen by templates.default / BuildingSpec.plan_template / GenBuilding.series; a footprint it cannot cut falls back to the S2.3 sections planner (recipes.block), then to the BSP. Plan frame as everywhere: u along the facade, v across, v = 0 = the court wall. A section = [flat A | tambour T | core K | flat C] along u; K (core.width_cm x core.depth_cm) and T (tambour_cm x core.depth_cm) stand on the court wall, flat B takes the street band over T + K (v = core depth .. D), A and C run the full depth. The core is a half-landing switchback: the floor landing (landing_cm) on the court side - the ground storey's court door opens onto it -, two flights per storey (each half the storey rise, 35 deg run) in two lanes, the mid landing (mid_landing_cm) at the far (inner) end; flats are entered from the landing (C) and from the tambour (A, B). A section under three_flat_min_depth_cm deep (the street band too shallow for flat B) is a two-flat section [A | K | C] (A and C full depth, both entered from the landing). Rooms on the 50 cm grid (designer 2026-11-20); every door keeps today's 150 cm (a door needs a 200 cm wall, so baths are 200 deep - the kit's 80 cm doors would allow 3 m2 baths: open question). Windows keep window_clear_cm (50, the kit's window grid in 3 m bays) from partitions and corners instead of the office's 120, so a 300 cm kitchen gets its window (the full window pass is a later step). Room areas: hall ~5-9, bath ~5-11, kitchen ~6-14, living ~9-35 m2 (room_area_m2 = the tolerance the TS tests check).

gable_door.comment: Designer decision 2026-11-22 (revised same day): a second exterior door (role entry) on an END wall (gable), ground storey only. ends = which gable gets it: 'low' (plan u = 0), 'high' (u = L), 'both' or 'none'; a block of both_min_sections sections or more gets both; BuildingSpec.gable_door overrides (a plan end or the draft side of a gable). The door opens into a SERVICE ROOM, not a flat: on the ground storey the whole end flat of the gable (its cells cannot be cut - the kitchen, bath and street living rooms all reach the gable, a partial flat would lose its kitchen) becomes a non-residential service bay (zone 'service', kind 'service', no unit): the cell on the gable at the court corner (the flat's kitchen cell) is the main service room, entered by the gable door, centred in its gable span on the 50 grid; its label is drawn from service_room.types by the plan seed; the flat's hall and corridor stay passages, the stair door (the flat's own entry) is the interior door to the section's tambour (three flats) or floor landing (two flats); the bath is a service WC, the street living rooms are annex rooms labelled from service_room.annex_labels. The upper storeys keep their three flats per landing unchanged; the ground storey of that section has two flats. plan.notes records it. state = the door's opening state (null = the generator's default for an exterior door; story 9 locks a gable door itself: building_stories.json gable_door_state).

balcony_slots.comment: Balcony / fire-escape slots (S2_ROOMS_PLAN.md 3.6, story 4): on every storey from min_storey the street-wall (v = D) windows of the rooms whose use is in uses get slot 'balcony' - add 'kitchen' to give street kitchens slots too. rate = the share of flat columns that get slots (drawn per flat from the plan seed, the same on every storey). A slot is only a marker: designer 2026-11-19 - no balcony without a fire escape, so nothing is built from it until story 4 turns one column's slots into balcony doors + balconies + the escape.

block_sections.comment: The S2.3 sections planner (S2_ROOMS_PLAN.md S2.3): flat core flat sections with a landing and lobbies; its numbers are recipes.block. Kept as a template and as the fallback of a footprint the kit planner cannot cut.
